operational_rules_learned_the_hard_way: backend `npm run lint` is `eslint --fix` and rewrites source. Gate on `npx eslint "{src,apps,libs,test}/**/*.ts"` instead.
Run backend unit tests as `TZ=UTC npm run test:unit`; some specs count periods against fixtures and flip under other offsets.
Jest here is v30: the flag is `--testPathPatterns` (plural).
Frontend `npm run test` takes ~9 minutes (628 files). Iterate with `npx vitest run <path>`; run the full suite once before pushing.

A FOREGROUND `sleep` IS BLOCKED in this sandbox, and so are chained short sleeps. To wait for a long job: start it with run_in_background, then start a second background job `until [ "$(ps aux | grep -c '[v]itest')" -eq 0 ]; do sleep 10; done` -- the harness notifies you when each exits.

NEVER git stash to check a test fails without the fix WHILE a full-suite run is in flight -- the running suite reads the reverted file mid-run and its result is worthless. Order: per-file revert checks FIRST, then start the full suite, then leave the tree alone.
Pipe a script's output to `head` and you can get a BrokenPipeError traceback AFTER the work already succeeded. Check the effect before believing the traceback.
NEVER write a SHA you have not read from git. Use `git rev-parse <short>`; a full SHA typed from memory is fabricated and lands in the coordination record.

A MOCK THAT DISCARDS AN ARGUMENT CANNOT TEST THAT ARGUMENT. Both currency findings (REV-015, REV-031) were invisible because the useNumberFormat mocks were `(amount) => ...`, dropping currencyCode, so a wrongly-labelled amount rendered identically to a correct one. Same class as the `{ data: [...] }` mock with no `pagination` that made fetchAllAccountTransactions throw while the component's swallow hid it. When a finding says 'X is not passed', check the mock honours X before writing the test, and mirror the real fallback (`code || default`).

The recharts mock in a chart's test file is often `YAxis: () => null, Tooltip: () => null`, which means the tick formatter and the tooltip content NEVER RUN -- no test can catch a formatting bug in either. Render their output in the mock, and have YAxis pass a tick INDEX as the second argument, because recharts calls tickFormatter as (value, index): `tickFormatter={formatCurrencyAxis}` by reference then silently receives 0 as its currency. `formatCurrencyAxis`'s `string | number` second parameter absorbs that instead of failing, which is why nothing flags it. Always wrap.

Prefer a REQUIRED prop over optional-with-default when threading a currency (or any per-entity identity). Required makes tsc enumerate every unfixed call site -- it found five in PayoffComparisonChart's test file -- and stops the next call site reintroducing the bug silently. CLAUDE.md ranks a compiler-enforced rule above a scanning test above prose.
transactions.status is NULLABLE (schema.sql:274). Never `status != 'VOID'` / `Not(TransactionStatus.VOID)`; use the entity's isVoid getter in JS or `(t.status IS NULL OR t.status != 'VOID')` in SQL.
Reuse an existing translated key across namespaces where the copy is identical. A new en-only errors.json key costs ~36 parity failures.

A nested withScopedDb JOINS the ambient transaction, so an assertXOwned helper opening its own withScopedDb still refuses before the caller's write. Findings written against pre-RLS code will ask for a QueryRunner manager -- there are none left in src/ and lint bans them.
createScopedDbMocks THROWS for an unregistered entity: adding a repository read means registering [Entity, mock] in the spec.
Verify every regression test by actually reverting the fix and re-running. Some tests deliberately pass either way; only the revert run tells those apart from vacuous ones.

vitest `import.meta.glob('/src/...', {query:'?raw', eager:true, import:'default'})` is how the guard tests read source. Pair every scanning assertion with a second one pinning the glob's match count, or a glob that matches nothing passes vacuously forever.
A finding's line number can be stale (REV-031 said 213, the call was at 384). Re-read and locate by content; never patch by line number.
